description: russia-colonialism techniques used by All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897), ATT&CK campaign C0067 (v1.2)
name: All-Russian Census and the Erasure of Identity (1897) (C0067)

techniques.comment: The denial to Ukrainians of the status of a separate people at the level of official doctrine. The linguist Sergei Bulich, in the article "Little Russian dialect" of the Brockhaus and Efron Encyclopedic Dictionary (1896), formulated: "The relation of the L[ittle] Russian dialect to the Russian language may be likened to the relation between the Slovak dialect and the Czech language… but not to the relation between the Polish, Czech, Serbian and similar languages, on the one hand, and Russian, on the other"(Citation: Малорусское наречие 1896) - by this classification Ukrainian was a dialect within the Russian language. This doctrine was applied to the entire empire by the Central Statistical Committee, which conducted the census of 1897: in the tables of the consolidated volume, "Little Russian" ran as a subdivision of a single "Russian language", and its speakers were counted into the overall total of "Russians"(Citation: Общий свод по Империи результатов разработки данных Первой всеобщей переписи населения, произведенной 28 января 1897 года. Т. 2 1905). This wrote 22,380,551 people into the "Russians" - speakers of the empire's second language after Great Russian (55,667,469)(Citation: Общий свод по Империи результатов разработки данных Первой всеобщей переписи населения, произведенной 28 января 1897 года. Т. 2 1905). Nearly one in four of them - 5,374,863 people - lived outside the nine Ukrainian governorates: in Voronezh governorate 915,883 people named Ukrainian as their native language, in the Don Host region (now mostly Rostov oblast of Russia) - 719,655, in Kursk governorate - 527,778, in Bessarabia (now Moldova and the south of Odesa oblast) - 379,698, in Grodno governorate (now western Belarus) - 362,526, in Stavropol governorate - 319,817, in Lublin and Siedlce governorates (the Kholm region and Podlachia, now eastern Poland) - 304,261, in Siberia - 223,274, of them 54,422 in the Amur and Primorye regions, in Akmolinsk region (now northern Kazakhstan) - 51,103(Citation: Общий свод по Империи результатов разработки данных Первой всеобщей переписи населения, произведенной 28 января 1897 года. Т. 2 1905). In the Kuban region (now mostly Krasnodar krai of Russia) Ukrainian was the most widespread native language: 908,818 people declared "Little Russian" (Ukrainian) as their native language against 816,734 with "Great Russian" (Russian), out of a regional population of 1,918,881(Citation: Общий свод по Империи результатов разработки данных Первой всеобщей переписи населения, произведенной 28 января 1897 года. Т. 2 1905). The census methodology also undercounted Ukrainians, notes the collective monograph of the Institute of History of Ukraine of the National Academy of Sciences: "The census of 1897 recorded not nationality but the respondents' native tongue, and since many Ukrainians named Russian as such, there were in fact more ethnic Ukrainians than indicated in the census"(Citation: Національне питання в Україні ХХ – початку ХХІ ст. 2012).
